overview: Sigma 4.11's Killaura is a full combat automation module driven entirely from the pre phase of EventUpdate, with EventRender3D reserved for ESP and EventStep for critical timing. One onEvent method branches on event type: the pre update picks a target (or a whole list in Multi mode), writes the aim into the outgoing movement packet via em.setYaw/setPitch, gates attacks on a per-tick timer (cps is re-rolled between the MIN/MAX APS settings every tick), and then either fires hitEntity or fakes a miss with a bare swing. Rotation is pluggable across Basic (instant snap), Smooth (yaw/1.7 easing), Legit (a nonlinear easing with a carried momentum term aacB) and Predict (one-tick velocity extrapolation), and the aura itself has Switch/Single/Multi/Multi2 target cycling, a Pre/Post attack-timing split, a hit-chance gate that also hard-misses when the needed yaw change exceeds an interval that shrinks with distance, and four autoblock flavors (NCP, Hypixel, Basic1, Basic2) that park the sword via a client-side itemInUseCount = 999 flag while the real block state is driven by C02 INTERACT + C08 placement packets. It also folds in a miniCrit integration that rewrites the movement packet's Y and onGround to manufacture fall-criticals whenever the Criticals module runs in Minis or HMinis mode.

sections.p: All logic lives in one @RegisterEvent handler listening for EventUpdate, EventRender3D and EventStep. The pre update first runs the death and respawn guards (toggle off when GuiGameOver shows or ticksExisted <= 1), then a conflict check that bails whenever BedFucker or CakeEater is mid block-break or Scaffold owns the look (Legit/Cubecraft/Custom with ROT), because those modules would fight Killaura for the rotation. Targeting is a two-pass sweep over mc.theWorld.loadedEntityList: getOptimalTarget(range) for the primary and blockTarget = getOptimalTarget(blockRange) for autoblock, each filtered by validEntity (distance, WALLS-gated visibility, AntiBot exclusion, friends, teams, invisibles, players-only) and ranked by sortList under the Angle/Range/FOV/Armor priority. In Single/Switch/Multi2 the chosen target is stored and the hit pipeline runs once per tick when timer >= 20/cps; Multi instead builds the full loaded list, aims at the first entry and sends one attack to every entry in the same tick. The post phase (TYPE=Post) runs the identical interval/hitchance gate on the post update, and blockTarget handling arms or parks the shield around it.

The rotation modes differ in how much of the required yaw is written per tick. Basic writes the exact rotation via em.setYaw/em.setPitch, so the movement packet that tick carries the full snap. Smooth steps yaw by targetYaw / 1.7 per tick. Legit uses customRots, a piecewise easing: yawFactor = targetYaw^2 / (4.7 * targetYaw) normally (targetYaw / 3.7 when the delta is under 5 degrees), and whenever the raw factor exceeds 7 it stores aacB = yawFactor * 7 and switches to targetYaw / 3.7, so the next tick adds the remembered momentum (yawFactor = targetYaw^2 / (6.7 * targetYaw) + aacB) -- an explicit attempt to break per-tick yaw-rate limits by splitting one large rotation across two packets. Predict aims at posX + (posX - lastTickPosX), one tick of extrapolation. getCustomRotsChange randomizes the aim point by +-0.3 blocks on x/z and -(0.4 + mult * randoms[1]) on y whenever the target is not inside the player's own bounding box, and bakes a -2.5 degree pitch bias into the returned delta. Independently of the rotation mode, shouldMiss is forced true when a random draw exceeds the HITCHANCE percent, when a new target was picked within the last 70ms (newTarget.delay(70)), while AutoPot is potting, or when the yaw still needed at attack time exceeds interval = 60 - distance * 10 (50 - distance * 10 in Legit), which collapses to near zero at max range; a miss still swings (swingItem) so the client-side animation and the server-side C0A both fire without an attack.

sections.h: Attack cadence and autoblock packet flow
sections.p: The attack gate is a tick counter, not a timer: timer increments every pre update and an attack fires when timer >= 20/cps, with cps re-rolled as randomNumber(min, max) between the MIN and MAX APS settings (both default 5, range 1-20), so at 20 APS one C02 ATTACK lands per tick and in Multi mode one per target per tick. hitEntity unblocks first if needed, fires the EventAttack hook around swingItem + playerController.attackEntity (the vanilla local attack so knockback and item damage simulate), then re-blocks in Basic1 mode. Autoblock is a three-packet sequence: with the INTERACT setting on, block() sends a C02 carrying a random Vec3 (x/z in +-0.5, y in 0-2.0) and a second C02 with Action.INTERACT, then a C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the held item; blockHypixel() swaps the C08 position for PlayerUtil.getHypixelBlockpos(username) with facing 255. The shield is represented client-side by forcing mc.thePlayer.itemInUseCount = 999, and unBlock() reverses it with syncCurrentPlayItem plus a C07PacketPlayerDigging RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN. The miniCrit hook rewrites the movement packet instead: in HMinis it cycles em.setY(posY + 0.0625 / 0.0626 / 0 / 0) with lastReportedPosY = 0 and setOnGround(false), and in Minis it staggers a 0.0628 offset off lastStep timing (the C04 it builds is commented out, so only the Y rewrite ships) -- the server sees the player fall ~0.06 blocks between hits and awards the fall-critical damage bonus.

files.label: Killaura.java (module)
files.explanation:
The constructor declares the full setting surface: RANGE (default 4.5, up to 8), BLOCKRANGE (up to 12), MIN/MAX APS (1-20), HITCHANCE, WALLS (on by default), INTERACT, AUTOBLOCK, TEAMS, INVISIBLES, ANIMALS, DEATH, TARGETMODE (Angle/Range/FOV/Armor), ROTATIONS (Basic/Smooth/Legit/Predict), AUTOBLOCKMODE (NCP/Hypixel/Basic1/Basic2), MODE (Switch/Single/Multi/Multi2), TYPE (Pre/Post) and ESP. onEnable snapshots the current yaw/pitch into the static sYaw/sPitch, records isBlocking from the vanilla isBlocking() state and seeds groundTicks; onDisable unwinds a parked shield (itemInUseCount == 999) with unBlock() so a disabled aura never leaves the client thinking it is blocking.

The onEvent dispatcher is where every combat decision happens. In the pre phase it runs the death/respawn toggles, the BedFucker/CakeEater/Scaffold conflict bail, target selection, rotation write, the timer >= 20/cps gate and the shouldMiss computation (line 400: neededYaw outside the 60 - distance*10 interval, newTarget under 70ms, or AutoPot potting forces a swing-only tick). Multi mode (line 236) aims at loaded.get(0) and then iterates the whole list firing EventAttack, a C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK and attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem per entity; the swing-only miss path still calls mc.thePlayer.swingItem() so the client animation is never empty. Switch mode re-rolls the target list every 400/500ms via switchTimer, and Multi2 cycles an index every attack tick. The blockTarget section (line 410) keeps the sword parked across ticks with itemInUseCount = 999 and dispatches block()/unBlock() by autoblock flavor, while the post branch (line 436) repeats the hit gate for TYPE=Post.

The helper block is the packet layer: hitEntity unblocks then swings and calls playerController.attackEntity (vanilla local damage path) before re-blocking; block() emits the C02+Vec3 / C02 INTERACT / C08 sequence; blockHypixel() emits C08 with PlayerUtil.getHypixelBlockpos(username) and facing 255; unBlock() emits C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN. getTargets/sortList rank by distance, FOV angle, absolute yaw difference, health or armor, and miniCrit (line 474) rewrites EventUpdate Y/onGround with the 0.0625/0.0626/0.0628 offset cycle, gated by groundTicks and the moveMods (Bhop/LongJump/Fly) enabled check.

files.label: RotationUtils.java (aim math)
files.explanation: This is the geometric core every rotation mode funnels through. getRotations aims at ent.posY + ent.getEyeHeight() / 2.0F, i.e. the vertical aim point is only half an eye-height above the target's feet, and getRotationFromPosition subtracts a hardcoded 1.2 from the player's Y before the atan2, so the pitch the module writes is consistently biased low relative to a true eye-line -- a constant, machine-like offset in the server-visible rotation. getPredictedRotations adds one tick of velocity (posX + (posX - lastTickPosX)) on x/z, which is exactly what the Predict mode writes into the movement packet. getYawChange and getPitchChange return the wrapped delta between the current look and the entity (getPitchChange carries the same -2.5 degree bias used by getCustomRotsChange), and these deltas are what Smooth (yaw/1.7) and Legit (customRots easing) consume each tick. canEntityBeSeen is the ray-cast the WALLS setting consults, and getDistanceBetweenAngles powers the FOV target sort. Because the same file is shared by the aim-assist and bow modules, its methods are the canonical aim vector source for the whole client.

files.label: Timer.java (tick-rate gate)
files.explanation: A 26-line millisecond stopwatch: delay(float milliSec) returns true once getTime() - prevMS reaches the argument and reset() re-anchors prevMS, with getTime() reading System.nanoTime() / 1e6 so it is monotonic rather than wall-clock. Killaura instantiates four of these: switchTimer drives the Switch mode cooldown (400ms, 500ms in Smooth rotation), newTarget enforces the 70ms grace after a target change that forces shouldMiss, lastStep is reset by the post EventStep to time the Minis critical offset, and rtimer is unused legacy. The module deliberately does not use this timer for the attack rate -- the cps gate is the EventUpdate tick counter (timer >= 20/cps), which is why the aura's attack interval is tied to game ticks rather than real milliseconds and stays exactly in phase with the movement packets.

countering.label: FightHitbox (combat hitbox ray trace)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's FightHitbox is the reach-and-hitbox check: MAX_REACH defaults to 3.1 (creative adds 1.9), and when a C02 lands the check defers the verdict until the next movement packet, because in 1.8 the yaw used for the hit-scan is one tick older than the attack. processDirection then takes the attacker's eye position (position + 1.62, minus 0.08 when sneaking), builds a ray from the yaw/pitch of that deferred move, fetches the victim's hitbox from the lag compensator at the attacker's ping (getHistoryLocation), expands it by BOX_EPSILON = 0.005, and punishes when the ray-box intersection lies more than maxReach from the eye. Occlusion is optional (CHECK_OCCLUSION defaults false), so wall-hits are only blocked when the server enables it.

Sigma's range setting defaults to 4.5 and tops out at 8, with BLOCKRANGE up to 12, so a default-config hit from 4.5 blocks has an interDistance of ~4.5 against a 3.1 ceiling: every attack in range 3.1-8 flags on the first punish. The Multi and Multi2 modes gain nothing here because each of the per-tick C02s is ray-traced independently. The WALLS=true default bypasses the (off by default) occlusion half of the check but not the reach half: the ray still intersects the victim box through the wall, and the intersection distance is still beyond 3.1. Lag compensation does not save the module either, because both positions are desynced in the same direction -- the victim is rewound to where the client saw it and the attacker eye is near-current.

countering.label: AimbotHeuristic (mouse-move pattern analysis)
countering.explanation:
AimbotHeuristic samples the 4 move packets after each click (MOVES_PER_SAMPLE = 4, MOVES_AFTER_HIT = 2) and scores the per-tick yaw/pitch deltas as 2D vectors. Three signatures punish: a stutter (maxSpeed - minSpeed > 4 with minSpeed < 0.01 and maxAngle < 0.1, i.e. a burst of near-zero rotation followed by a sudden move), a twitch or zigzag (two consecutive moves over 20 degrees each with a turn of more than 2.86 rad), and a jump discontinuity (speed - lastSpeed < -30 with a turn over 0.8 rad, i.e. a huge rotation that stops dead). It is cancelless and only feeds VL, and its own docs call it easily bypassed, but it flags a large fraction of stock auras.

Sigma's Basic mode writes the entire rotation to the movement packet in one tick -- a target behind the player produces a 180-degree snap followed by near-zero moves, which is precisely the jump-discontinuity signature. Smooth eases at yaw/1.7 per tick and Legit's customRots caps |yawFactor| at 7 with the aacB momentum carry, so their per-tick deltas stay bounded, but the stutter branch fires when the cap engages (the carried momentum appears as a stalled move right before the hit). Switch and Multi2 re-pick targets every 400-500ms and flip the yaw sign between opposing targets, feeding the zigzag branch. Because the module always swings on misses too, the click window around every swing is scored, not just the hits.

countering.label: Angle (fight.angle multi-target ledger)
countering.explanation:
NCP's fight Angle check keeps a 1-second ledger (maxTimeDiff = 1000ms) of every attack location and scores four averages over it: average move between consecutive hits (avgmove < 0.2 blocks adds 20 * (0.2 - avgMove) / 0.2), average time between hits (avgtime < 150ms adds 30 * (150 - avgTime) / 150), average yaw change per hit (avgyaw > 50 degrees adds 30 * avgYaw / 180), and target-switch rate (each hit on a different entity whose yaw jumped more than 30 degrees adds 20 * avgSwitching). The largest term over its config threshold (angleMove/angleTime/angleYaw/angleSwitch) fires; otherwise angleVL decays by 0.98. It is the classic forcefield check and its four terms map onto Sigma mode by mode.

Multi mode sends one C02 to every entity in range within the same tick, so consecutive ledger entries have zero movement between them: avgmove sits at 0 and the violationMove term alone is 20 per pair of hits, immediately over the default threshold. At 20 APS the per-tick attacks land 50ms apart, which is under the 150ms avgtime bound and adds 30 * (150 - 50) / 150 = 20 per pair. Switch mode re-picks targets every 400-500ms and Basic rotation snaps the yaw to the new target in one packet, so any two targets more than 30 degrees apart in yaw contribute deltaSwitchTarget entries; a single multi-target fight with standing players scores avgmove + avgtime + switchspeed simultaneously and the check cancels the hits.

countering.label: KillAura (fight.killaura direction/reach/speed)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's KillAura check runs on every combat event with defaults max-direction-angle 1.2 (radians), max-swing-time 80ms, max-reach 4.2, max-attacks 16/s and max-attack-packets 20/s. Direction computes the 3D angle between the server-side look direction and the vector to the attacked entity; Reach measures distance from the player to the entity's position minus its velocity; NoSwing fires when more than 80ms elapsed since the last ARM_ANIMATION (C0A) packet; Speed counts every USE_ENTITY packet (interact and attack alike, incremented in PacketListener for all C02s) against max-attacks per second, and checkFrequency counts ATTACK-action C02s against max-attack-packets.

The Reach default is the sharpest cut for Sigma: range defaults to 4.5 (max 8), so an out-of-the-box 4.5-block hit already exceeds 4.2 and flags, and the setting's whole upper half is unusable under default config. Speed is a close second: at 20 APS the module sends 20 ATTACK C02s per second, right at the max-attack-packets ceiling, and with the INTERACT setting on each block()/hit cycle adds two more C02s (vector interact + INTERACT), so totalAttacks easily exceeds 16/s even at moderate APS. NoSwing and Direction are the two checks the module passes: every hit is preceded by swingItem (C0A arrives within the 80ms window) and the rotation is written into the movement packet that same tick before the C02 is flushed, so the server-side look matches the attack vector. The practical bypass surface is to keep APS at or under 15 and range under 4.2 with INTERACT off -- which is exactly what the default settings are not.

countering.label: CombatListener (use-entity pipeline + transaction desync)
countering.explanation:
In this Spartan snapshot (the ai.idealistic line, CheckEnums wiring the KILL_AURA and HIT_REACH hacks to their check classes), CombatListener is the USE_ENTITY pipeline: onPacketReceiving resolves the target entity id against online players, fires a PlayerUseEvent into the combat checks for every ATTACK action, and records the attack in a pendingAttacks map (an OverflowMap capped at 1024 entries). The map is drained onPacketSending when the server's damage event for that entity arrives, and a pending attack that outlives the matching transaction is flagged through isSDesync() with the message 'attack faster than the transaction response' -- Spartan's rate check is keyed to the transaction echo, not to a fixed APS ceiling.

That transaction anchor is the relevant counter for Sigma's burst shapes. Multi mode emits N C02 attacks in a single tick, and at 20 APS the module sustains 20 attacks per second, while the transaction stream is one server response per tick: bursts of simultaneous C02s cannot each have a distinct transaction predecessor, so the pendingAttacks map accumulates entries that never drain in order, and the desync path reports attacks arriving faster than the transaction responses. The combat event that CombatListener fans out also feeds the hitbox validation (RayUtils.inHitbox ray tests) that the HIT_REACH hack is wired to in CheckEnums, which is where the module's 4.5-8 block default range is caught by the server-side hitbox intersection instead of the client's own claim.
